questions.q: According to Friedman, what is government's primary role?
a: Uphold the law and keep order
Own the main industries
Set wages and prices
Manage the flow of credit
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the state should enforce the law and preserve order rather than interfere with individual freedom.

questions.q: Why does Friedman doubt that stimulus spending can fix a crisis?
a: It arrives too late, after the crisis has passed
It gives too much money to the rich
It causes immediate runaway inflation
It forces interest rates to rise
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the political process is so slow that stimulus lands after the downturn it was meant to address.

questions.q: What did stimulus money do during the Great Depression, according to the summary?
a: People saved it instead of spending it
It went mostly to large banks
It created a wave of inflation
It was spent on foreign imports
questions.why: Lesson 2 notes that government intervention led people to hold onto the extra money rather than spend it.

questions.q: What does Friedman propose to replace existing welfare programs?
a: A negative income tax
A higher minimum wage
Public housing for every family
A universal basic income
questions.why: Lesson 3 suggests scrapping inefficient programs and giving federal aid to anyone below a minimum earnings level.

questions.q: What problem does the summary name with public housing?
a: It shrinks the housing supply and confines the poor
It costs far more than private housing
It gives tenants too much choice
It pushes landlords to raise rents
questions.why: Lesson 3 says bureaucrats run public housing poorly, reducing supply and trapping poor residents in unsafe areas.
